full_judgment: 5. Further, a deed of gift being a 'Hiba' followed by delivery of possession is for all practical purposes a deed under Transfer of Property Act read with relevant provisions of Muslim Personal Law. Provisions of sections 10 and 11 of the Transfer of Property Act are applicable in the present case. Under section 10 of Transfer of Property Act where a property is transferred subject to any condition or limitation absolutely restraining the transferee from parting with or disposing of his interest in the property, such condition and limitation is void. Under section 11 of the Transfer of Property Act where on a transfer of property, an interest therein is created absolutely in favour of any person, but the terms of transfer direct that such interest shall be applied or enjoyed by him in a particular manner, he shall be entitled to receive and dispose of such interest as if there was no such direction. Chapter 7 of the Transfer of Property Act relates to "gift" in general and section 129 thereof states that it shall not effect any rule of Mohammedan Law. Muslim Personal Law also speaks about the provisions of gift very explicitly. In this connection reference may be made to Mulla's Principles of Muhammedan Law, eighteenth edition, by Mr. Hidayatullah. Section 160 thereof says that gift of an undivided share in any property which is capable of division is irregular and it may be perfected and rendered valid by subsequent partition and delivery to the donee of the share given to him. Section 161 further says that a gift of property which is capable of division to two or more persons without specifying their shares or without dividing it is invalid but it may be rendered valid if separate possession is taken by each donee of their respective portion of the property or if there is subsequent arrangement between the donee with regard to the possession of the property. Section 164 further says that when a 'gift' is made subject to a condition which derogates from the completeness of the grant, the condition is void, and the gift will take effect as if no conditions were attached to it.
